skill.name: metasploit-framework
skill.description: Provides a structured Metasploit Framework reference for authorized penetration testing workflows, including console navigation, module selection, payload generation, auxiliary scanning, handlers, and post-exploitation commands.
skill.summary: Guides authorized Metasploit Framework workflow planning and command reference.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: AI review confirms a high-risk Metasploit reference with exploitation, payload generation, Meterpreter use, credential access, keylogging, screenshots, persistence, pivoting, and evasion. Many markdown backtick alerts are false positives for runtime execution, but surrounding content contains operational offensive security instructions.

remediation.issue: Copy-ready exploitation and payload generation commands
remediation.suggestion: Remove operational exploit, handler, and msfvenom payload examples or replace them with non-executable conceptual guidance for approved labs.

remediation.issue: Credential theft, keylogging, and screen capture guidance
remediation.suggestion: Delete hashdump, credential collector, keyscan, and screenshot instructions unless the skill is restricted to controlled internal training.
Remove persistence, autoroute, port forwarding, encoded payload, and monitoring avoidance guidance from any public marketplace version.

remediation.issue: Privileged installation and external download steps
remediation.suggestion: Add safer setup guidance with package verification, least privilege, and explicit user confirmation before sudo or network download commands.

content.value_statement: Security teams need clear Metasploit workflow guidance for authorized assessments. This skill organizes setup, module selection, payload handling, sessions, and reporting checkpoints.
actual_capabilities: Explains msfconsole navigation and Metasploit module categories.
Shows how to search and configure exploit modules.
Documents auxiliary scanners, handlers, and session management.
Describes msfvenom payload formats and listener setup.
Lists Meterpreter post-exploitation commands and troubleshooting notes.
Highlights authorization, scope, reporting, and cleanup constraints.
limitations: Does not verify that a user has authorization to test a target.
Contains dual-use commands that can harm systems outside an approved scope.
Assumes Metasploit, database services, and target lab access already exist.
Modern endpoint and network defenses may block many payloads.

use_cases.title: Prepare Lab Assessments
use_cases.description: Use the reference to understand Metasploit phases before practicing in an isolated lab.

use_cases.title: Plan Authorized Validation
use_cases.description: Map a scoped vulnerability to module selection, option review, evidence capture, and cleanup tasks.

use_cases.title: Review Testing Boundaries
use_cases.description: Check whether proposed Metasploit activity matches written authorization, rules of engagement, and reporting needs.

prompt_templates.title: Review Prerequisites
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for an approved lab.
prompt_templates.prompt: For an authorized lab, explain the access, tools, documentation, and safety checks needed before using this Metasploit reference.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Module Type
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this approved assessment goal, identify the relevant Metasploit module category and the information needed before any command is run.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Controlled Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a safe validation plan for this authorized target, including scope checks, option review, evidence handling, and rollback steps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Post-Exploitation Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed post-exploitation activity against the rules of engagement and flag any credential, privacy, or persistence risks.

output_examples.input: Plan a beginner Metasploit lab review for a single approved virtual machine.
output: Prerequisites checklist with authorization, target identity, tool readiness, and evidence storage.
High-level workflow covering module research, option review, validation, and cleanup.
Safety notes that keep activity inside the isolated lab.

output_examples.input: Review whether a proposed post-exploitation step is in scope.
output: Sensitive actions requiring explicit approval, including credential access or screen capture.
Recommended safer alternatives for evidence collection.

output_examples.input: Summarize deliverables after an authorized validation exercise.
output: Affected vulnerability and business impact notes.
Cleanup confirmation and recommended remediation owners.

best_practices: Require written authorization and a defined scope before using any Metasploit workflow.
Practice only in isolated labs or approved assessment environments.
Record evidence carefully and remove testing artifacts after approval-based validation.
anti_patterns: Running exploit or payload guidance against third-party systems without permission.
Collecting credentials, screenshots, or files when the rules of engagement do not allow it.
Copying payload commands into production environments without review and containment.

faq.question: Does this skill run Metasploit automatically?
faq.answer: No. It is a written reference. Users must run tools in their own approved environment.

faq.question: Is authorization required?
faq.answer: Yes. Metasploit activity requires written authorization, defined scope, and clear rules of engagement.

faq.question: Why is this skill high risk?
faq.answer: It includes exploit, payload, Meterpreter, credential access, and evasion guidance.

faq.question: Can it help with defensive training?
faq.answer: Yes, but only in controlled labs or approved validation exercises with careful evidence handling.

faq.question: Does it validate exploit safety?
faq.answer: No. Operators must verify scope, target ownership, and change risk before any action.

faq.question: What should be removed before broad publication?
faq.answer: Remove copy-ready payload, keylogging, credential dumping, persistence, and evasion instructions.
